title: 1952 AHSME Problem 43
statement: The diameter of a circle is divided into \(n\) equal parts. On each part a semicircle is constructed. As \(n\) becomes very large, the sum of the lengths of the arcs of the semicircles approaches a length:

answerChoices.label: A
answerChoices.text:
Equal to the semi-circumference of the original
circle

answerChoices.label: B
answerChoices.text: Equal to the diameter of the original circle

answerChoices.label: C
answerChoices.text:
Greater than the diameter but less than the semi-circumference
of the original circle

answerChoices.label: E
answerChoices.text: Greater than the semi-circumference but finite

solutions.text:
Each small semicircle has diameter \(\frac{d}{n},\) so its arc length is \(\frac{\pi d}{2n}.\) The sum of all \(n\) arc lengths is \[ n\cdot\frac{\pi d}{2n}=\frac{\pi d}{2}, \] exactly the semi-circumference of the original circle. This equality holds for every positive \(n,\) not merely in the limit.

Thus, the correct answer is A.
hints: Let the original diameter be \(d\), so each small semicircle has diameter \(\frac{d}{n}\)
Multiply the arc length of one small semicircle by the number \(n\) of parts
